premises.text: Retailers face an analytical divide and cannot make fast competitive pricing decisions across tens of thousands of SKUs against online rivals without losing profitability
premises.evidence_span: There's a huge analytical divide. Retailers just don't have the firepower to make quick decisions for all their products

premises.text: Boomerang is a dynamic price-optimization platform (not mere price matching) connected to the retailer's e-commerce stack for competitive positioning and strategy setting
premises.evidence_span: We are a price optimization company

premises.text: What-if simulation uses historical data to project revenue and profit before a pricing strategy is submitted
premises.evidence_span: Before I hit submit, I want to simulate a what-if strategy. Boomerang has looked up the past historical data and has given me some projections in terms of revenue and profits

premises.text: SaaS monetization via monthly subscription fees
premises.evidence_span: We are a SaaS product, which means we monetize with monthly subscription fees

value.text: Dynamically price e-commerce items for competitiveness and profitability
value.evidence_span: dynamically price your items for competitiveness and profitability

causal_links.evidence_span: An average retailer is just not able to compete in this new world of e-commerce

notes: Sales-lift traction and booking numbers excluded as performance metrics. Dashboard UI steps folded into price-optimization premise; what-if simulation retained as a distinct learnable capability that could fail independently. Partition is need/product/money triad; justified because subscription pricing is revisable without changing the optimization engine, and the analytical-divide problem is a separate market assumption. Singleton D1 and D3 noted accordingly.
